review.summary: Harrington's own MPSA for a $210k US healthcare analytics engagement involving patient data. The draft is heavily one-sided toward the client: uncapped daily liquidated damages, uncapped contractor liability, one-way indemnity covering the client's own negligence, 90-day payment terms, termination-for-convenience with no pay for work in progress, and assignment of even AtliQ's pre-existing IP. Cyber insurance required ($5M) exceeds AtliQ's current cover ($1M). Patient data triggers HIPAA/BAA requirements not yet evidenced in this bundle. One possible register conflict (Crestline MFN) depends on facts not in this document.

review.summary: BlueOrchid pilot (USD 38,000, 16 weeks) for AI-based guest review analytics across 12 hotels, including properties in Dubai and Muscat. Commercial terms (payment, LD cap, liability cap, mutual indemnity, IP, confidentiality) broadly match AtliQ's past positions. However, the scope directly overlaps with AtliQ's live non-compete owed to Al Noor Hospitality, which bars AtliQ from providing data analytics/AI services to any Hospitality Business with GCC properties. Guest data from Gulf properties also raises unaddressed regulated-data questions, and no NDA/MSA/SOW paperwork is evidenced.

register_conflicts.incoming_clause_quote: BlueOrchid wishes to run a time-bound pilot of an AI-based guest review analytics solution across its entire portfolio
register_conflicts.register_clause_quote: the Supplier undertakes that neither it nor any of its Affiliates shall, during the Restricted Period, directly or indirectly, provide data analytics, artificial intelligence or revenue-management services to any Hospitality Business in the GCC.
register_conflicts.explanation: BlueOrchid operates hotels in Dubai (UAE) and Muscat (Oman), both GCC states, and the Pilot is expressly an AI-based data analytics service. This falls squarely inside the restricted scope of the live Al Noor non-compete (term runs to 2028, tail to ~2029) and no waiver exists for BlueOrchid.

register_conflicts.explanation: AtliQ explicitly reaffirmed to Al Noor in 2026 that the GCC hospitality non-compete still applies to every other hospitality business in Oman/GCC. BlueOrchid's Dubai and Muscat properties fall within that reaffirmed restriction, with no consent obtained.
